Topic 2.1: Crop Establishment • Preparing Planting Site • Planting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Crop Establishment • Preparing Planting Site • Planting, part of FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES Strand Sub strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why do we prepare a planting site before planting? 2. How do you prepare a planting site?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Crop Establishment • Preparing Planting Site • Planting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner develops observation skills as learnt relate size of planting materials to type of tilth.

● Self-efficacy: The learner develops leadership skills when they share and carry out tasks in groups when preparing planting sites and

establishing crops.

Values:
● Unity: As a learner cooperates with others while preparing planting sites and establishing crops.

● Responsibility: As a learner shows determination when performing roles and duties assigned during group activities to prepare planting

sites and establish crops.

17

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security: The learners observe safety and security for self and others as they use garden tools and equipment to prepare planting

sites and establish crops.

Link to other learning areas:

• The learner relates the concept of safety and security for self and others a concept from Pre-Technical Studies as they use garden tools

and equipment to prepare planting sites and establish crops.

• Learners relate planting site (tilth) and seed size to concept of germination learnt in Integrated Science.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Seeds from different crops of various sizes.

• Print reference materials.

• Digital devices.

• Medium sized seeds such as maize grains, beans.

• Large planting materials like tubers, suckers and cuttings.

• Suitable planting sites such as walls of buildings, fence lines, driveways in schools, suitable containers.

• Manure.

• Garden tools and equipment such as jembes, pangas, slashers, watering cans, wheelbarrow.
